identity.title: World Action Models are Zero-shot Policies
identity.repo_note: Official inference and training code, shallow-cloned at this commit. Checkpoints were not downloaded.

summary: DreamZero fine-tunes a pretrained video diffusion backbone to denoise future video latents and robot actions together. The released training path is a causal Wan model: one DiT sees video tokens and action registers, and the loss is a weighted MSE on both velocity targets. The paper's main model is Wan2.1-I2V-14B. The class defaults opened in CausalWanModel are a smaller shape, so those defaults are not the 14B width. Closed-loop inference replaces predicted frames with the real observation in the KV cache after each chunk.

landscape.paradigm: Joint video-action diffusion, a 14B world-action model
landscape.bottleneck: Physical-motion generalization of VLAs that only imitate actions
landscape.hardware_fit: Local note: not recommended, about 40–80+ GB. The paper's speed table uses H100 and GB200.

data.note: DROID and AgiBot episodes were not downloaded. The sample fields are the tensors WANPolicyHead.forward reads. Volumes are from the paper.

datasets.name: AgiBot G1 teleop
datasets.volume: About 500 hours, 7.2k episodes, 22 environments. Episodes average about 4.4 minutes and about 42 subtasks. Video is sampled at 5 fps and actions at 30 Hz, horizon 48, which is 1.6 seconds per chunk.
datasets.sampling: Idle actions are filtered. Relative joint positions are the default action. Training samples a trajectory and splits it into M=4 chunks of K=2 latent frames.
datasets.augmentation: The data transform package includes crop, color jitter, and related video transforms. Which of those the 14B run enabled was not confirmed in the training config.

training_provenance.summary: AgiBot and DROID training use recorded teleoperated episodes. The model is trained to match the logged action chunk and the video.

model.overview: A Wan video DiT with action and state registers. The VAE, image encoder, and text encoder stay frozen. The DiT, state encoder, action encoder, and action decoder train. CausalWanModel is the backbone class. Its __init__ defaults (dim 2048, 32 layers, 16 heads, ffn 8192) are not the Wan2.1-I2V-14B shape; the 14B width is selected by the checkpoint config.

total_params.name: Backbone
total_params.value: 14B for the Wan2.1-I2V-14B runs. A 5B Wan ablation is also reported. Added parameters are the state and action encoder/decoder.

modules.name: CausalWanModel
modules.detail: Autoregressive DiT. Class defaults are a smaller config and must not be read as the 14B width.

modules.name: WANPolicyHead
modules.detail: Encodes video, prompt, and image, noises both modalities, and returns the sum of weighted MSEs.

modules.name: Frozen encoders
modules.detail: Text encoder, image encoder, and VAE are frozen.

model.runtime: AST outline is in extracts/model_outline.txt (75 Module-like classes). The 14B checkpoint was not downloaded and the model was not constructed.

compute.name: Main training
compute.value: 100k steps, global batch 128, separately for AgiBot and for DROID. The GPU count of that run was not extracted. Ablations use 50k steps and batch 32.

compute.name: Inference speed
compute.value: The paper's table: system optimizations about 9x on H100 and about 16x on GB200; DreamZero-Flash reaches 38x on GB200, 5.7 s down to 150 ms, about 7 Hz. The README also quotes about 0.6 s on GB200 and about 3 s on H100 with DiT caching.

objectives.name: Shared interpolation
objectives.explanation: Clean latent and clean action sit at t=1. Noise sits at t=0. In the default objective a chunk shares one timestep across video and action. DreamZero-Flash draws them separately: video time from Beta(7, 1), action time uniform.

symbols.meaning: Clean VAE latent of the video chunk.

objectives.name: Joint velocity loss
objectives.explanation: The target velocity is the clean pair minus the noise pair. Context C_k is the clean previous chunks (teacher forcing). The opened implementation splits this into a weighted video MSE plus a weighted action MSE, and gates the action term with the action mask and has_real_action.

symbols.meaning: Clean latents and actions of earlier chunks.

train.text: Encode the clip with the frozen VAE and the prompt with the frozen text encoder. Normalize uint8 video into [-1, 1].
Split the trajectory into chunks. Sample a timestep. Unless Flash decoupling is on, video and action share it.
Interpolate toward noise, run the causal DiT on the noisy latent and the noisy action, and add the weighted video MSE to the weighted action MSE.
Teacher-force the previous chunks as clean context. Update the DiT and the action/state heads. Leave the text encoder, image encoder, and VAE frozen.

infer.text: The server converts the observation and calls the causal joint video-action sampler.
Denoise the next video chunk and action chunk. Execute the action chunk.
After execution, write the real observation back into the KV cache in place of the predicted frames.

task.embodiment: AgiBot G1 teleop and a Franka robot on DROID.
task.action: Relative joint positions normalized to [-1, 1]. AgiBot uses 48 action steps at 30 Hz. DROID uses 24 action steps at 15 Hz.
task.horizon: Both settings cover 1.6 seconds. Training packs M=4 chunks of K=2 latent frames. Closed-loop inference writes the real frame back into the KV cache.
task.contact: Video, text, proprioception, and action. A wrench input was not recorded.
task.latency: DreamZero-Flash is reported at about 7 Hz on GB200, 5.7 s down to 150 ms. The README also quotes about 0.6 s on GB200 and about 3 s on H100 with DiT caching.
task.data: AgiBot is about 500 hours and 7.2k episodes. DROID is a separate 100k-step run. Video is sampled at 5 fps.

parts.outputs: Video tokens and a text embedding for the DiT.

parts.trained: The DiT and the state encoder.
